key_insight: In small exact simulations, fixed-angle QASPA-MaxCut achieved group-mean selection ratios of 0.955–1.000, exceeding the reported depth-one QAOA mean scores.
engineering_relevance: The results motivate studying how shallow quantum circuits and classical search budgets jointly affect practical Max-Cut performance.
method: Encode graph edges with CX–Ry(θ)–CX shift-phase blocks.
Evaluate the four leading QASPA bit strings classically and retain the best cut.
Compare against locally optimized depth-one QAOA with one to ten restarts.
evidence_signal: Seed-42 exact state-vector tests covered backbone-augmented random graphs at four edge probabilities and 19 custom unweighted topologies; retained finite-shot checks left topology-level readouts unchanged.
watch_item: QASPA’s best-of-four selection score and QAOA’s expected approximation ratio are different metrics, so the reported gap does not establish a like-for-like advantage or hardware scalability.
paper_title: QASPA-MaxCut on Unweighted Graphs: Edge Encoding and QAOA Restarts
